w: A gilded Independent Man crowns the fourth-largest self-supporting stone dome on Earth, McKim, Mead & White's neoclassical statehouse on Smith Hill. The House sits in the west wing, the Senate in the east, alongside the governor and other state offices. Listed on the National Register since 1970.
s: A gilded Independent Man tops the fourth-biggest dome
_facts: Designed by McKim, Mead & White in neoclassical style
Fourth largest self-supporting stone dome in the world
Topped by the gilded 'Independent Man' statue
Houses the Rhode Island General Assembly and state executive offices; NRHP since 1970

w: Brown University's second-oldest library building opened in 1910 across from the Van Wickle Gates and became the campus's main library, displacing the building later renamed Robinson Hall. One of five libraries in the University Library today, the Hay holds Brown's rare books, manuscripts, and University Archives.
_facts: Second-oldest library on Brown University's campus, built 1910
Located on Prospect Street opposite the Van Wickle Gates
Became the campus's main library, replacing what is now Robinson Hall
Holds rare books, manuscripts, University Archives, and special collections

w: Richard Upjohn, the architect who defined American Gothic Revival churches, raised this one at Westminster and Mathewson Streets in 1845-46. It has anchored downtown Providence for over 175 years, added to the National Register in 1972 as part of the Downtown Providence Historic District.
_facts: Historic Episcopal church at Westminster and Mathewson Streets
Built 1845-1846, designed by Richard Upjohn in Gothic Revival style
Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1972
Part of the Downtown Providence Historic District

w: The first independently funded private library ever placed on a US university campus, the John Carter Brown holds rare books, manuscripts and maps on European exploration and colonization of the New World to about 1825. It sits on Brown's campus but is funded separately from the university library system.
s: The first private library built on a US campus
_facts: Independently funded research library on Brown University's campus
Collections cover European exploration and colonization of the New World to c.1825
First independent private library placed within a US university campus
Holds rare books, manuscripts, and historical maps

w: A 427-acre landscape named for the man who founded both this city and the colony around it: Roger Williams. Laid out as an elaborately designed park, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places as a historic district in its own right, its grounds now also home to the Roger Williams Park Zoo.
_facts: 427-acre elaborately landscaped city park
Named for Roger Williams, founder of Providence and Rhode Island
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places as a historic district
Grounds include the Roger Williams Park Zoo

w: Founded in 1872, this is the third-oldest zoo in the United States and, in 1986, became the first zoo in New England accredited by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums. More than 800 animals across upwards of 100 species live within Roger Williams Park, next to the Carousel Village.
_facts: Founded 1872, third-oldest zoo in the United States
First zoo in New England accredited by the AZA, 1986
More than 800 animals from over 100 species
Located within Roger Williams Park, near Carousel Village
